title: The Locked Room
image_alt: A Victorian bedroom at night: shuttered window, a bell-rope hanging beside the bed, a small grille high on the wall and a dark wardrobe.
intro: Stoke Moran, April 1883. Helen Stoner's sister died in a bedroom locked from the inside. The windows were barred, the door was bolted, and the chimney was too narrow for a child. Her last words were: 'It was the band! The speckled band!' Two years later, Helen has been moved into that same room, and she has begun to hear a low whistle in the dark.
teaser: A sealed bedroom, a dying cry about a speckled band, and a whistle in the night.
objective: Discover what the speckled band really was.
watson_greeting: Stoke Moran, Holmes's old case. Helen Stoner's sister died in this very room, behind a bolted door and barred shutters. Look around, and ask me anything about the case papers.

hotspots.name: The bell-rope
hotspots.observation: A thick bell-pull hangs beside the pillow. Give it a tug: it rings nothing. It is not attached to any wire, only fastened to a hook just above the little opening of the ventilator.
hotspots.note: The bell-rope is a dummy. It rings nothing and is fixed to a hook next to the ventilator.
hotspots.quote: it is not even attached to a wire

hotspots.name: The ventilator
hotspots.observation: A small grille high on the wall. Strangely, it does not open to the outside air: it leads into the next room, Dr. Roylott's bedroom.
hotspots.note: The ventilator opens into Dr. Roylott's room, not to the outside air.
hotspots.quote: what a fool a builder must be to open a ventilator into another room

hotspots.name: The bed
hotspots.observation: The bed will not move an inch. It is clamped to the floor, so whoever sleeps here always lies in the same place: beside the rope, beneath the ventilator.
hotspots.note: The bed is clamped to the floor and always sits under the rope and the ventilator.
hotspots.quote: It was clamped to the floor

hotspots.name: The shuttered window
hotspots.observation: Old-fashioned shutters with broad iron bars, secured every night. Holmes tried every way to force them open from outside, without success.
hotspots.note: Nobody came in through the window: the shutters are barred every night.
hotspots.quote: old-fashioned shutters with broad iron bars, which were secured every night

hotspots.name: Box of matches
hotspots.observation: A match-box beside the lamp. Julia Stoner was found holding the charred stump of a match in one hand and a match-box in the other: she had struck a light to see something in the room.
hotspots.note: Julia struck a match the night she died: something was in the room with her.
hotspots.quote: In her right hand was found the charred stump of a match, and in her left a match-box

hotspots.name: Walls and floorboards
hotspots.observation: The coroner had the walls sounded and the flooring examined. Everything was solid: there is no hidden passage into this room.
hotspots.note: No secret passage: walls and floor are solid.
hotspots.quote: The walls were carefully sounded, and were shown to be quite solid all round

clues: The bell-rope beside the bed is a dummy. It is not attached to any wire and rings nothing at all.
The bed is clamped to the floor, so it can never be moved away from the rope.
In Dr. Roylott's room there is a safe, a saucer of milk, and a dog lash tied into a loop of whipcord.
suggested_questions: What happened to the bell rope?
Why was the bed clamped to the floor?
What did Holmes find in Dr Roylott's room?
riddle:
I am no band of cloth, though a band they named me.
I crossed no floor, for the floor I never touched.
I came down the rope that rang no bell,
and returned to the hand that set out milk.

What am I?
solution_note: It was a swamp adder, the deadliest snake in India. Dr. Roylott sent it through the ventilator and down the dummy bell-rope, and called it back with a whistle and a saucer of milk.

title: The Stolen Jewel
image_alt: A study in Baker Street on a snowy night: a battered felt hat and a white feather on the table, papers, a wicker hamper by the fire and an empty leather armchair.
intro: London, the 27th of December. The Countess of Morcar has lost the blue carbuncle from her jewel-case at the Hotel Cosmopolitan. A plumber named John Horner has been arrested and swears he is innocent. Meanwhile, a commissionaire named Peterson has brought Holmes a battered hat and a Christmas goose, picked up in a scuffle on Tottenham Court Road.
teaser: A countess's gem vanishes, a plumber is arrested, and a battered hat turns up with a Christmas goose.
objective: Discover where the stolen gem was hidden.
watson_greeting: Baker Street, the second morning after Christmas. Peterson left a battered hat and a goose here, and the papers are full of the Countess of Morcar's jewel. Holmes's chair is empty. Shall we look at what he left on the table?

hotspots.name: The battered hat
hotspots.observation: A hard felt hat, cracked, very dusty and spotted. The red silk lining is discoloured, and the initials 'H. B.' are scrawled on one side. A card on the goose read 'For Mrs. Henry Baker'.
hotspots.note: The hat and the goose belong to a Henry Baker ('H. B.').
hotspots.quote: the initials "H. B." were scrawled upon one side

hotspots.name: Newspaper cutting
hotspots.observation: 'Hotel Cosmopolitan Jewel Robbery.' John Horner, plumber, is charged. James Ryder, upper-attendant at the hotel, gave evidence that he had shown Horner up to the Countess's dressing-room on the day of the robbery.
hotspots.note: James Ryder, upper-attendant, is the man who took Horner to the dressing-room.
hotspots.quote: James Ryder, upper-attendant at the hotel, gave his evidence

hotspots.name: Poultry hamper
hotspots.observation: A hamper lined with straw. The goose came through a chain of hands: the Alpha Inn's goose club, the salesman Breckinridge of Covent Garden, and before him a supplier, 'Mrs. Oakshott, 117, Brixton Road, egg and poultry supplier.'
hotspots.note: The goose's trail: Alpha Inn, then Breckinridge of Covent Garden, then Mrs. Oakshott of Brixton Road.
hotspots.quote: Mrs. Oakshott, 117, Brixton Road, egg and poultry supplier

hotspots.name: A white feather
hotspots.observation: A single white feather. In the Brixton Road yard, one bird was picked out of the flock with care: a fine big one, white, with a barred tail. And there were two barred-tailed birds that could not be told apart.
hotspots.note: Someone chose a white goose with a barred tail, and there were two identical ones.
hotspots.quote: a fine big one, white, with a barred tail

hotspots.name: Holmes's armchair
hotspots.observation: Still warm from the fire, but empty. Wherever Holmes has gone, he left this case open on the table for someone to finish.

clues: Peterson's wife found the blue stone when she opened the bird in her kitchen.
The bird Ryder chose was white, with a barred tail, from a flock in a back yard on Brixton Road.
James Ryder, head attendant at the Hotel Cosmopolitan, had shown Horner up to the dressing-room that day.
suggested_questions: What did Peterson bring to Holmes?
Where did the Alpha Inn get its geese?
riddle:
A plumber stands charged, and the stone is gone.
Yet that night the jewel slept inside something living:
white, with a barred tail, and bound for a Christmas table.

Where did the gem lie hidden?
solution_note: James Ryder forced the stone down the throat of a goose, into its crop. He picked the wrong bird from the flock, and the gem travelled to Tottenham Court Road inside it.

title: The Secret Vault
image_alt: A bank cellar under brick arches: a great round vault door, iron gates, stacked crates, a lantern on a crate beside loose papers, and a stone-flagged floor.
intro: Saxe-Coburg Square. Jabez Wilson, a pawnbroker with flaming red hair, was paid four pounds a week to sit in an office and copy the Encyclopaedia Britannica by hand. This morning he found the door locked and a card announcing that the Red-Headed League is dissolved. His assistant, who offered to work for half wages, is nowhere to be found.
teaser: A league that pays red-headed men to copy an encyclopaedia, and an assistant who works for half wages.
objective: Discover what the assistant was really doing in the cellar.
watson_greeting: We are underground, in the cellar of a City bank next to Jabez Wilson's pawnshop. Mind the lantern. Look at the crates and the floor, and ask me about the League.

hotspots.name: Holmes's case notes
hotspots.observation: Holmes's notes on Jabez Wilson's story. For eight weeks the League paid him to copy the Encyclopaedia Britannica by hand: 'Abbots and Archery and Armour and Architecture and Attica'. From ten to two, every day, away from his shop.
hotspots.note: The League kept Jabez Wilson away from his shop for four hours every day.
hotspots.quote: I had written about Abbots and Archery and Armour and Architecture and Attica

hotspots.name: The vault door
hotspots.observation: This is the cellar of the City branch of one of the principal London banks. Above, through the streets, is Saxe-Coburg Square and Wilson's shop.
hotspots.note: This cellar belongs to a City bank branch.
hotspots.quote: in the cellar of the City branch of one of the principal London banks

hotspots.name: The crates
hotspots.observation: The bank borrowed 30,000 napoleons in French gold and never unpacked them. This crate alone holds 2,000 napoleons packed between layers of lead foil.
hotspots.note: There is a fortune in French gold lying in this cellar.
hotspots.quote: contains 2,000 napoleons packed between layers of lead foil

hotspots.name: The flagstones
hotspots.observation: Mr. Merryweather strikes his stick on the flags that line the floor, and looks up in surprise: 'Why, dear me, it sounds quite hollow!'

hotspots.name: The lantern
hotspots.observation: With this lantern and a magnifying lens, Holmes knelt on the floor and examined the cracks between the stones. A few seconds were enough for him.
hotspots.note: Holmes studied the cracks between the floor stones, not the vault door.
hotspots.quote: with the lantern and a magnifying lens, began to examine minutely the cracks between the stones

hotspots.name: The iron gate
hotspots.observation: The way down to the cellar passes a massive iron gate and a flight of winding stone steps that ends at another formidable gate. Nobody gets in this way unseen.
hotspots.quote: a flight of winding stone steps, which terminated at another formidable gate

clues: The assistant was willing to work for half wages, and spent hours every day down in the cellar.
The knees of his trousers were worn, wrinkled and stained.
Holmes thumped the pavement outside the shop with his stick, and the Coburg branch of the City and Suburban Bank backs onto Wilson's premises.
suggested_questions: Why did Holmes beat the pavement?
What did Holmes see on the assistant's trousers?
What was next to the pawnbroker's shop?
riddle:
The league was a fiction, the copying a pretext,
designed only to empty a shop for four hours a day.
The assistant asked for half wages and spent them underground,
and his knees told the story his mouth did not.

What was he digging?
solution_note: John Clay, under the name Vincent Spaulding, was burrowing a tunnel from the cellar of the pawnshop into the vault of the City and Suburban Bank next door.
